method: Whole-file manual reading of keyboard and mouse hook implementations; exact-commit downloads matched pinned Git blob IDs. Hooks not installed or executed.
findings: Each matching profile queues an independent ThreadPool callback with original mutable profile reference, captured delegate and window handle; no bounded queue, cancellation token or callback drainage on Stop/Dispose. Already queued work can outlive hook stop.
Multiple profiles sharing keys all trigger; keyboard IsHandled is assigned per match, so last matching profile decides final handling value. Mouse handler does not use profile.IsHandled here.

Explorer foreground check is cached once within event iteration. A later Global profile can inherit handle populated by earlier Explorer-scoped match; a Global profile before that match receives0. Profile order affects captured handle context.
Mouse double-click check uses fixed500ms, same button and TickCount subtraction; no position tolerance or system double-click setting. Triple clicks can mark both second and third as double clicks.
Background delegate exceptions are not caught in these callbacks. No per-profile revalidation occurs at execution time; changed enabled/action/path values can be observed through mutable reference.
Dispose calls stop then dependency disposal without local disposed guard or unsubscribe; dependency idempotence and callback lifecycle not qualified.
limits: No original H.Hooks dependency runtime, Windows input, timing or hook lifecycle tests performed. No input simulation executed or production code adopted.
